units.title: Review title and scope
units.summary: The title identifies this source as an adversarial review of the kernels document.
units.context_reason: This title establishes authorship and scope for the review assertions that follow.

units.title: Executive assessment and priority corrections
units.summary: The review attributes strengths and failures to the source, then identifies FAT, Mercury, Phantom-GRAPE, warp, propulsion, dust, and clock issues.

claims.proposition: FAT capability claims must be checked against a pinned release because the review reports that current documentation does not implement several named solvers and drag.

assumptions.text: The review accurately characterizes the cited evidence and the target source version.

verification.evidence_needed: A pinned FAT release, module inventory, and executable examples for each asserted solver and force model.

claims.proposition: The review says Mercury must distinguish Hamiltonian switching from package-level RADAU availability.

assumptions.text: The review accurately represents the cited source and target version.

verification.evidence_needed: Chambers method description and Mercury source.

claims.proposition: The review identifies a mismatch between the displayed laser-sail equation and the source table values.

assumptions.text: The review accurately represents the cited source and target version.

verification.evidence_needed: Independent four-momentum calculation and dimensional analysis.

claims.proposition: The review says warpax percentages require version, domain, and sampling qualifications.

assumptions.text: The review accurately represents the cited source and target version.

verification.evidence_needed: Matched metric and grid reproduction.

claims.proposition: The review identifies a weak-field clock-sign problem under negative-potential convention.

assumptions.text: The review accurately represents the cited source and target version.

verification.evidence_needed: Weak-field and Minkowski limit derivation.

claims.proposition: The review identifies the White-torus energy and mass-equivalence entry as dimensionally contradictory.

assumptions.text: The source table transcribes both quantities correctly.

verification.evidence_needed: A direct conversion of the stated mass equivalent to joules.

learning_goals.goal: Distinguish a review assertion from its target claim and record the evidence needed to decide both.

units.title: FAT implementation review
units.summary: Reviews FAT solver and force-model implementation claims.

claims.proposition: The review says FAT claims for Nyström, Adams, and drag need a pinned release because the inspected public documentation did not substantiate all of them.

assumptions.text: The review accurately identifies the documentation and version it inspected.

verification.evidence_needed: Pin the reviewed FAT release and compare its solver and perturbation inventory with each source claim.

claims.proposition: The review says the common prograde modified-equinoctial formulation remains singular at retrograde inclination i = π, despite the source’s nonsingularity wording.

assumptions.text: The cited equinoctial convention and retrograde limit apply.

verification.evidence_needed: Derive the element-map denominator at inclination π and compare it with the source wording.

learning_goals.goal: Pin the FAT release, audit each listed solver, and derive the stated retrograde singularity.

units.title: NBODY and gyrfalcON review
units.summary: Reviews collisional N-body architecture and conservation claims.

claims.proposition: NBODY architecture claims need hardware-qualified benchmarks, and gyrfalcON force conservation does not prove all integration invariants.

assumptions.text: The review and target source refer to identifiable releases.

verification.evidence_needed: Reproduce benchmarks and isolated-system invariant tests.

learning_goals.goal: Assess the evidence and limits of nbody and gyrfalcon review.

units.title: Mercury hybrid review
units.summary: Reviews encounter switching and solver attribution.

claims.proposition: Mercury must distinguish Chambers Hamiltonian switching from separately available encounter integrators.

assumptions.text: The review and target source refer to identifiable releases.

verification.evidence_needed: Compare the Chambers method with Mercury source and encounter tests.

learning_goals.goal: Assess the evidence and limits of mercury hybrid review.

units.title: Phantom-GRAPE review
units.summary: Reviews SIMD implementation versus projected AVX-512 claims.

claims.proposition: Documented AVX2 kernels must be distinguished from projected or architecture-dependent AVX-512 claims.

assumptions.text: The review and target source refer to identifiable releases.

verification.evidence_needed: Inspect versioned kernels and measure named CPUs.

learning_goals.goal: Assess the evidence and limits of phantom-grape review.

units.title: Einstein Toolkit review
units.summary: Reviews numerical-relativity release and component claims.

claims.proposition: Einstein Toolkit component claims require release-qualified documentation because its infrastructure evolves.

assumptions.text: The review and target source refer to identifiable releases.

verification.evidence_needed: Inspect a pinned thorn inventory and release notes.

learning_goals.goal: Assess the evidence and limits of einstein toolkit review.

units.title: Warp tooling and statistics review
units.summary: Focused review of warp tooling and statistics review.

claims.proposition: Warp diagnostic percentages require fixed metric, domain, resolution, observer set, and version.

assumptions.text: The cited review evidence applies to the source configuration.

learning_goals.goal: Evaluate evidence and limits for warp tooling and statistics review.

units.title: Warp propulsion and steering scope review
units.summary: Focused review of warp propulsion and steering scope review.

claims.proposition: Radiative steering is conditional and does not establish reactionless propulsion.

assumptions.text: The cited review evidence applies to the source configuration.

verification.evidence_needed: Derive its flux law under stated junction conditions.

learning_goals.goal: Evaluate evidence and limits for warp propulsion and steering scope review.

units.title: Shielding and dust review
units.summary: Focused review of shielding and dust review.

claims.proposition: The review says a 10^-9 kg silicate sphere would have a radius near 49 μm rather than the source’s 5 μm interpretation.

assumptions.text: The review uses the stated silicate density and spherical-grain model.

verification.evidence_needed: Recalculate radius from mass and density, and state whether radius or diameter is compared.

claims.proposition: The review agrees that a 10^-9 kg grain at 0.5c has kinetic energy about 1.39 × 10^7 J but rejects the associated 5 μm size label.

assumptions.text: The mass and speed are 10^-9 kg and 0.5c.

verification.evidence_needed: Recalculate relativistic kinetic energy and TNT equivalence independently of the size conversion.

learning_goals.goal: Recalculate the grain radius, kinetic energy, and TNT equivalent as separate checks.

units.title: Ramjet review

learning_goals.goal: Evaluate evidence and limits for ramjet review.

units.title: Force and clock convention review
units.summary: Focused review of force and clock convention review.

claims.proposition: The review says the weak-field clock correction has the wrong sign if Φ is the conventional negative Newtonian potential.

assumptions.text: The conventional negative-potential sign is used.

verification.evidence_needed: Evaluate the expression for Φ < 0 and compare it with the standard weak-field proper-time limit.

claims.proposition: The review requires force-frame labels and limiting-case tests for coordinate and proper acceleration handoffs.

assumptions.text: The handoff equations mix coordinate and proper quantities.

verification.evidence_needed: Test zero velocity, zero gravity, and constant proper-acceleration limits with explicit frame labels.

learning_goals.goal: Evaluate the weak-field sign and test each acceleration handoff in named frames and limiting cases.
